final.question: What do you do with what's left over?
final.form: Her own ferment log — date started, salt, days checked, when it's ready — stretched into eight chapters named Started, Logged, Dated, Salted, Checked, Ready, Tasted, Opened
final.object: Seven to nine plain glass jars, same size and shape, a blank label on each face — at rest, her jar wall

swap.reason: It is built on this kitchen's own ferment log fields, the specific jar wall strangers stop to ask her about, the koji cupboard she calls a cupboard, and Callum's bins line — not on generic chef material.

backdrop.reason: The jars carry the timeline, the log fields, the photographs, the links and the figures, so removing them removes the page's structure rather than an ornament.

depth.reason: Eight chapters follow the arc of a single entry — one blank jar, labelled, placed in time, salted, checked, ready, tasted, opened — and the order cannot be shuffled.

clipart.reason: The central object is a labelled preserving jar from her own larder, not the stock emblem of a chef (hat, knife, plate).

honesty.reason: Fjaerland is stated as a ten-week stage washing and labelling jars, the waste figure is attributed to the whole kitchen over one month in 2023 with bones excluded, September 2022 is used for Head Chef, Priya is credited on screen and Olu's drawings are held out.

thirty_seconds.reason: The first screen gives name, role and the question, with a skip-to-the-answer link to the close (answer plus apply/book/write/read links) and a chapter rail that jumps straight to the proof chapters.

plain_reader.reason: "Ines Okafor. Head Chef, Saltmarsh, Leeds. What do you do with what's left over?" reads plainly to an outsider and states nothing a kitchen insider would wince at.

judgement.summary: A one-page scroll built from Ines's own ferment log, in eight chapters, with a set of seven to nine labelled glass jars as the single 3D object that moves from one jar to a row of places and years, to the jar wall as a photo grid, to three tipped-out figure cards, and back to the whole wall answering "what do you do with what's left over? You keep it." Its weakest spot is the two chapters that carry the site's actual purpose — the apprentice and workshop links sit on jars holding plain text and no content, because the agent correctly refused to invent what either involves, so the pages that matter most to the intended visitors are the thinnest on the page.
